head.title: UnplugLock: Lock Your Laptop When the Charger Is Unplugged
head.description: Free Windows app that locks your laptop the instant the charger is pulled, so whoever grabs it gets a lock screen, not your email and accounts.
head.ogDescription: If someone pulls the charger to grab your laptop, Windows locks straight away, so they get a lock screen instead of your accounts.
head.ogImageAlt: A laptop showing the Windows lock screen, with its charging cable pulled out
ld.description: Free tray app for Windows that locks your laptop the moment the charger is unplugged, so whoever grabs it gets a lock screen instead of your signed-in accounts.
ld.feature1: Locks Windows when the laptop switches from AC power to battery
ld.feature2: Optional lock delay of 1 to 10 seconds
ld.feature3: Can also lock when Ethernet is unplugged or Wi-Fi disconnects
ld.feature4: Password protection with a recovery code
ld.feature5: Guard process that restarts the app if it is closed
lang.label: Language
hero.lede: A tiny, free Windows app. If someone grabs your laptop off the charger, they get a lock screen, not your accounts.
hero.laptopLabel: A laptop on charge, signed in to an online banking page. As you scroll, its screen tilts up, the charging cable is pulled out of the side, and the screen switches to the Windows lock screen.
mock.code: 482 913 is your bank security code. Never share it.
steps.1body: UnplugLock sits in the system tray and watches the power cable.
steps.2body: At the wall or at the laptop, it doesn't matter.
steps.3body: Instantly, or after a short delay you choose.
tray.label: UnplugLock's right-click menu in the Windows system tray
tray.heading: Lives in the tray
tray.delayBody: Lock instantly or after 1–10 seconds, so a loose cable doesn't lock you out.
tray.networkBody: Optionally lock when the Ethernet cable is pulled or Wi-Fi disconnects, so a laptop running on battery is covered as well.
tray.hardBody: Set a password to stop anyone else turning it off or closing it.
tray.hideBody: Hide the tray icon and UnplugLock keeps running out of sight. Open it again from the Start menu to bring the icon back.
tray.signinBody: Locking only helps if Windows asks for a password, PIN or Windows Hello. If your account has none, UnplugLock tells you.
tray.adminBody: Installs and runs as your normal user. Right-click the icon for settings.
faq.grabbed: What happens if someone grabs my laptop while it's charging?
faq.grabbedA: To grab a charging laptop they have to pull the charger out first. The moment it drops to battery, UnplugLock locks Windows, so they're stuck at the lock screen instead of inside your email, browser and accounts.
faq.unplugged: What if my laptop isn't plugged in?
faq.unpluggedA: Turn on the network locks. Right-click the tray icon, open Also lock when, and pick Ethernet is unplugged, Wi-Fi disconnects, or both. Then Windows also locks when someone pulls the network cable or carries the laptop out of Wi-Fi range. Both are off by default, because switching Wi-Fi networks yourself locks too.
faq.password: Do I need a password on my Windows account?
faq.passwordA: Yes. UnplugLock locks the screen, but if your account has no password, PIN or Windows Hello, anyone can click straight back in. Set one up in Settings → Accounts → Sign-in options.
faq.alarm: Does it sound an alarm when the laptop is unplugged?
faq.alarmA: No. Instead of an alarm it locks Windows, the same as pressing Win + L, so your files and accounts stay protected.
faq.kensington: Is it an alternative to a Kensington lock?
faq.kensingtonA: Not really, they do different jobs. A Kensington lock physically stops someone walking off with your laptop. UnplugLock can't do that, but if someone does take it, they're stuck at the lock screen instead of going through your photos, emails and accounts. If you've got a cable lock, use both.
faq.files: Does it keep my files safe if the laptop is stolen?
faq.filesA: It keeps whoever took it out of your signed-in session: your email, browser, apps and everything you had open. To protect the files on the drive as well, even if someone takes the drive out, turn on BitLocker or Device encryption in Windows settings. The two work well together.
faq.windows: Does it work on Windows 11 and Windows 10?
faq.windowsA: Yes. It runs on Windows 11 and on Windows 10 from the April 2018 Update onwards, using the .NET Framework that's already built in. It doesn't need admin rights.
faq.freeA: Yes. It's free and open source under the MIT licence, with no account, no ads and no internet connection.
faq.privacyA: No. There's no telemetry, analytics or tracking of any kind, and UnplugLock never connects to the internet, so nothing about you or your laptop is ever sent anywhere. Its settings stay on your laptop, and the code is open source if you'd like to check.
faq.close: Can a thief just close it?
faq.closeA: Not easily. With a password set it can't be turned off or exited without the password, and a guard process restarts it within about a second if it's closed. It's a deterrent rather than a guarantee, though: someone with admin rights who knows what they're doing can still stop it, so use a strong Windows password too.
support.heading: Support UnplugLock
support.body: UnplugLock is free, with no ads and no paid version, and it'll stay that way. If it's useful to you, you can chip in whatever you like to help keep it going.
